KRYteria

Knowledge. Relationships. You.

Relationships are complicated. Standards are not.

Christine Little · MGT 409 AI Foundations · kryteria.onrender.com

1
The problem

Somebody deciding whether to keep going.

Four months into dating someone. A friendship that has started costing more than it gives. A boundary at work that keeps getting crossed. The question is always the same one: was that a problem, or was it me?

They are not short of information. The evidence is scattered across months of memory, the standard they set in January has quietly moved by June, and the friend they keep asking has started agreeing with them to end the conversation.

The failure is not knowing. It is acting consistently with what you already know.

2
What it is

A decision mirror

It compares three things: what you say you want, what you are actually experiencing, and what you are choosing to do about it.

1 — Hold the standard

Your criteria, written once and kept, each carrying its importance within a profile.

2 — Read what happened

Write the messy version. The agents separate what happened from what you concluded, and map each observation to the criteria it bears on — supporting, contradicting, or complicating.

3 — Hand the record back

State a conclusion and it answers with your own entries, including the ones that cut against you.

And four things it will never do. No compatibility score · No stay-or-leave recommendation · No judgment of your standards · No diagnosing anyone or assigning a definitive label. It challenges your reasoning, never your standards.

3
What is different

The real incumbent is not a product

A general-purpose chatbot, a Notes app, and advice from friends.

KRYteria Evaluates experiences against individually defined criteria

The claim is not that these cannot discuss a relationship — it is that persistent, independently configurable criteria and evidence-based assessment are the organizing architecture here.

The Jimmy G Principle

Importance belongs to a criterion within a profile. Status is what is known about one person against it. The two are independent, and that is the architecture, not a joke.

Importance, per profileHusbandOne night
Financial independenceMandatoryAspirational
Physical attractionPreferredMandatory
Wants childrenMandatoryset aside

Same person. Different profile. Different criteria. The person has not changed; the objective has. No profile ranks above another — enforced in the data model, and in an interface that pre-selects none of them.

Set aside is not a fourth tier. Importance and status are separate columns on separate tables, and so is the flag that takes a criterion out of one profile.

4
How it works

A controlled workflow, not a chat mesh

Seven specialists; the orchestrator routes and makes no model call of its own.

Narrative and Safety run concurrently on the raw text, so no mapping can normalize something before the safety layer sees it — and the safety layer takes no profile argument, asserted by a test that reads the function signature.

Reasoning is handed what Evidence decided, and is expected to disagree with it.

5
One real run

The entry that contained what changed

A live brain dump, chosen to be hard: a writer stating flatly that nothing has changed.

AgentInOutLatencyCost
narrative2,8851,0752.2 s

evidence1,7211,9730.3 s

Total10,6926,14632.0 s$0.0037

Reasoning is the expensive agent by a distance — 22.5 seconds and more output than everything else combined. It ran because she stated a conclusion, and it is the only agent whose job is to disagree with one.

Five agents here because she asked for reflection; an ordinary entry runs three, at $0.0027. What it saved, on screen: 3 entries support this · 1 cuts against it, with the counterpoint named, two alternative explanations, and what is still unknown.

6
Tokenomics

Measured, not estimated

Per brain dump$0.0027
100 users / mo$3.27
10,000 users / mo$327
Spent building it$0.248

The cost-cutting step, and what it cost us. Routing is the cost control. The first version keyed on a keyword list and saved money by not doing the thing the product is for: across 36 corpus entries it fired 4 times, and only 3 of 13 adversarial cases reached the agent written to test them.

Routing on stated conclusions instead costs +53% per entry — $162.88 to $249.62 at 10,000 users. Worth it.

An ordinary entry is three agents; a full run is five, at $0.0044 — $524 at 10,000 users. Both ends measured 21 Nov, and both went up about 28% in a week because every fix to the product’s judgment is a permanent addition to the prompt. Behavior is bought with tokens, and the bill recurs. 22 live runs · 404 measured calls · 915,972 input / 359,603 output tokens, at $0.10/$0.50 per 1M. Per-account and global daily token caps are enforced in the orchestrator, in code. Cache writes are not modeled, so figures are slightly low on a cold cache.

7
Safety

Record everything. Withhold the analysis.

What the layer found, unprompted

An ordinary demo entry. Nobody labeled anything, and no criterion mentions safety. Classified physical / potential / note only:

He repeatedly pressed after you said you needed to leave and stood between you and your bag, using humor to make objecting feel difficult… That is worth taking seriously; you do not have to decide what to call it.

No diagnosis, no legal conclusion, nobody labeled. Over-response is graded as a failure here exactly as minimization is.

The other kind of safety

Argon2id, CSP, cross-account rows that 404 rather than 403 — and account creation bounded for the whole app, because the per-handle throttle cleared on success, so a fresh handle met no limit and ~17 of them exhaust the daily token budget for everybody.

The defense, and the test holding it

A halt is a presentation decision, not a recording one. Being grabbed and prevented from leaving is a behavior; refusing to write it down leaves the record emptiest at the point it matters most.

Narrative, themes, Evidencerun and persist
Reasoningskipped — a deposition
Reflectionskipped — not reflective here
The screenacknowledgment, a safety check you can answer, resources — nothing else

The code shipped the other way once: the orchestrator returned before the save, so the entry a user was most serious about was the one KRYteria recorded least. A test now asserts the halt is set before the save, and that it is read from code — never off the model's own suggested action, which comes from the same call that classified the concern.

8
Impact

Measured against how this is done today

Not "users felt better". The claim: KRYteria makes a person's own inconsistency visible, and nothing they use today does — same entries, same model, prose only, so our structure earns no points.

A general-purpose chatbot, fair prompt

That sounds exhausting — especially if you've repeatedly been left handling things you thought you could count on him for. What happened most recently that brought this up?

Warm, reasonable, blind to all three of her prior entries.

KRYteria, same entry

How do you reconcile that conclusion with the earlier notes that he was on time for dinner, rescheduled a day ahead, and texted when he was leaving on the late occasion?

Counter-evidence from her own record, by entry id, unprompted.

Produced at allKRYteriaChatbot Prose score across six dimensions
Evidence mappings · contradicting or complicating2 · 20 · 0 5–3 on the contradiction scenario, 4–4 on the flattering one. The chatbot failed the two dimensions it structurally cannot do: naming the standard at stake, and surfacing the record.
Questions raised · traceable to entry ids2 · yes0 · no

Who would carry it: a university student-support or wellbeing program, as one optional self-reflection tool. Not therapy, not a crisis service, not a counselor. 10,000 students ≈ $330/month.

Then real people opened it. "I've clicked through all of them. But I don't really know where to start." — Alex M., 34, New York. With no criteria, Evidence never runs — his two entries came back with nothing to act on. Every check passed on that build. Deborah L., 70, Massachusetts, found the opposite door: she could not get out of a demo, because signing out lived in Settings. Neither is a missing feature — both are a route that existed and was never shown.

9
Limits & next steps

Stated, not discovered

  • Governments cannot keep their own hotlines accurate. One service contradicted itself about its own number. If accuracy is the value proposition, that is our decay rate too.
  • Observations record whose conduct they describe. An entry about his own habits once returned 25 rows of doubt about her, lifted from his own criteria. Now 4, nothing lost.
  • One research entry stays pending. Rounding the number up would be the most corrosive thing anyone could do to that layer.
  • The hosted instance keeps nothing, and says so above the sign-up form. It was in three files and said to nobody — documented is not disclosed.

Next

  • The user test, then a second on a non-romantic domain.
  • Migrations before anybody's journal depends on it; resources re-verified on a schedule, not before a deadline.

Nothing to type: click a character and you are in. A free instance sleeps after fifteen minutes, so the first load takes about a minute — the screen says so rather than looking broken.

KRYteria does not validate conclusions. It validates your right to examine them.
